initialSetup.title: Manual - Amnimo Test Runner
initialSetup.desc: This manual explains how to use Amnimo Test Runner step-by-step.
initialSetup.heading: Initial Setup
initialSetup.subheading: When you first start Amnimo Test Runner, you need to set the path to the test source code folder (amnimo-e2e). This is required for the software to locate test data.
initialSetup.step1: Start app: Start Amnimo Test Runner from desktop or start menu.
initialSetup.step2: Path request: A message prompts you to set the root path (e2e path).
initialSetup.step4_1: A system window appears. Navigate to the drive and folder where the amnimo-e2e project is saved.
initialSetup.step6: The application validates and saves this path. This step will be skipped on next startup.

page.title: Sessions Management
page.desc: The main screen of Amnimo Test Runner is where you manage Sessions. This section explains how to create a new session in detail.
page.heading: Create a New Session
page.step1Desc: Click the "New Session" button at the top right of the dashboard, or the add button in the session card area.
page.step2Desc:
A dialog "New Test Session" appears.

Enter a memorable name (e.g. AG10-v3.8.0-release) and click "Create Session".
page.step3Desc: The new session appears in the list and the screen automatically navigates to the setup screen.
page.noteDesc:
Even if you exit at step 3 without finishing setup, the created session is saved and displayed on the dashboard with a DRAFT tag.

You can click the Setup button on the session card anytime to return to the setup screen and resume the process.

page.title: Session Setup
page.desc: After creating a new session, you need to configure it before running tests. This process involves specifying the test execution type, target device, environment settings, and environment checks.
page.heading: Open Setup Screen
page.openSetupDesc: When you create a new session, it automatically navigates to the setup screen. Alternatively, click the "Setup" button from a DRAFT session card on the session dashboard.
page.typeDesc: Select the scope and type of tests to run.
page.typeRelease: Release Test: Comprehensive suite for release certification. Runs in full test order.
page.typeSystem: System Test: Select specific functions to test. Ideal for focused verification.
page.typePlayground: Playground: Flexible environment for experimental testing. Skips environment checks.
page.typeNote: Note: If you select "Playground", you do not need to execute the "4. Environment Check" step.
page.deviceDesc: Select and enter the device to test and its connection info.
page.deviceBoard: Device Series and Board: Select the target board from the list. For boards with multiple types, select the type as well.
page.deviceUrl: Base URL: Enter the URL to access the GUI of the target device. (e.g. https://192.168.0.254)
page.envDesc: Check and configure the contents of the .env file for this test run.
page.envDevice1: SERIES, BOARD, TYPE: Automatically set from the previous step and cannot be changed here.
page.envDevice2: PREV_FIRMWARE_NAME: Automatically populated from the staging and production servers.
page.envDevice3: TEST_FIRMWARE_NAME: Automatically populated from the staging server. You can select a different firmware from the dropdown list.
page.envNetwork1: PC_SERVER_URL, PC_SERVER_PORT: Click the server icon on the right to open the list of running IIS servers. Select the server to use for downloading firmware later.
page.envNetwork2: DHCP_CLIENT_IP: Enter the IP address of the GW used as the DHCP client. (e.g. 192.168.3.254)
page.envNetworkNote: When preparing the GW for the DHCP client, you must set an IP address with a different subnet than the target device and INTERNET_ADDRESS.
page.envConst1: CLI_SERVER_PORT: Select the port for the CLI server. When running tests on multiple devices simultaneously, choose a port not used by other sessions.
page.envNote: For other items, refer to the hints displayed in each form to prepare the environment.
page.checkDesc: Verify if the local environment is ready for testing.
page.check1: Connection Status: The application automatically pings the "Base URL" entered in Step 2 to confirm GUI accessibility.
page.check2: SIM Check: Automatically sends an API to the device to confirm a SIM card is correctly inserted in slot 0.
page.check3: Storage Device: Automatically sends an API to confirm USB and SD cards are inserted.
page.check4: Nx Witness: Automatically checks if the Nx Witness web client is accessible. Click the 'Web Client' button to open it and complete device registration.
page.check5: PoE Camera: Automatically sends an API to confirm the PoE camera is connected to the correct LAN port.
page.check6: DHCP Client (Partner GW) Check: Automatically pings the DHCP Client GW IP configured in Step 3 for connectivity. Then sends an API to check if DHCP4 is enabled.
page.check7: FW File Prep: Displays the firmware files required for testing. If files do not exist locally or on the server, click download to retrieve them. If they exist on the server but not locally, click 'Sync from server', or 'Sync from local' for the reverse.
page.completeDesc: When all items in Step 4 are in a "check successful" state, the "Complete & Go to Runner" button becomes active. Click it to proceed to the test execution screen.
